case.title: The Cold Cocoa Cart
case.hook: Remember Rosa’s ice cream cart on the boardwalk? In December it sells hot cocoa at the Palmetto Beach Lighted Boat Parade. This year Rosa switched to shiny new metal mugs. Now her order slips are full of complaints. What went wrong?

menu.name: Rosa’s Cocoa Cart
menu.sub: Lighted Boat Parade · Saturday, 6 to 9 PM

items.t: Hot cocoa in our NEW shiny metal mug

menu.note: Tonight: 54°F by the water. Bring a jacket!

slips.t: My cocoa was cold before the first boat went by!
Ouch! The mug handle was too hot to hold.
Last year your foam cups kept my cocoa hot all night. What happened?

stills.alt: A fishing boat covered in colorful holiday lights, with a lit-up tree and candy canes, sails past at night.

case.stillsCredit: Light Boat Parade at John’s Pass, Madeira Beach, Florida: Richard Mc Neil, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
case.question: Why does Rosa’s cocoa go cold so fast in the new metal mugs, and why do the handles get hot?
case.how: Find 4 clues as you work through the lesson. Then crack the case (solve it) at the top of the Assignment tab.

clues.where: Warm-Up: three spoons in a mug
clues.t: Metal carried the cocoa’s heat all the way up the spoon handle. The wood and plastic handles stayed cool.

clues.where: The Lesson, Part 1: be the heat
clues.t: Heat moves from the warmer thing to the cooler thing. Hot cocoa gives its heat to the cold night air. Cold never flows in.

clues.where: The Lesson, Part 2: the butter rod race
clues.t: Metals are conductors: heat moves through them fast. Glass and wood are insulators: they slow heat down.

clues.where: The Lesson, Part 3: the Cup Race
clues.t: The metal cup cooled the fastest. The foam cup kept its water warm the longest.

solve.title: What went wrong at the cocoa cart?
solve.q: Which answer fits all four clues?

options.t: The cold night air flows into the metal mugs and makes the cocoa cold.
options.why: Check Clue 2. Cold doesn’t flow. Heat flows OUT of the cocoa into the cooler air.

options.t: Metal is a conductor. It carries the cocoa’s heat out into the cold air and up into the handle. A mug made of an insulator, with a lid, would keep the cocoa hot.
options.why: Case cracked! Metal moves heat fast, so the cocoa cooled and the handles got hot. Insulators slow heat down.

options.t: Metal mugs are just colder than other mugs, even on the same cart.
options.why: Check Clue 3. Metal isn’t colder. It moves heat faster, so heat leaves the cocoa faster.

options.t: Rosa didn’t make the cocoa hot enough.
options.why: Check Clue 4. In the Cup Race, every cup started with the same warm water. The metal one still cooled the fastest.

heatdots.title: Be the heat
todo: Drag a 🔴 heat dot from the warmer thing to the cooler thing (or press Send).
Try “Send cold”, too.
Keep going until they are the same temperature. Then do round 2.

why.t: Each red dot stands for a little bit of heat. More dots means warmer. This is a model.

heatdots.coldNo: Nothing moved. There is no such thing as a “cold dot”. Cold just means LESS heat.
heatdots.wrongWay: That dot bounced back. Heat only moves from the WARMER thing to the COOLER thing.

rounds.line: Your hand is warmer than the ice. Drag a heat dot from your hand to the ice, or press Send.
rounds.done: In this model, heat moved from your hand INTO the ice until they matched. That’s why your hand felt cold: it was losing heat. (In real life your body keeps making heat, and the ice melts.)

rounds.line: The cocoa is warmer than the night air. Send its heat dots out.

b.bigNote: The night air is HUGE, so the heat dots barely warm it.

rounds.done: The cocoa cooled down to the air’s temperature. The air hardly changed. Cold air never flowed IN. Heat flowed OUT.

opts.t: From the warmer thing to the cooler thing.
From the colder thing to the warmer thing.
Both ways at the same time.
opts.miss: Could you drag a dot from the ice back to the hand?

heatdots.win: Heat only moves from warmer to cooler. Cold never flows. Clue 2!

rodrace.title: The butter rod race
todo: Pick 3 rods.
Predict: drag each butter dot onto 1st, 2nd or 3rd (or tap it, then a place).
Press “Heat the ends” and watch.

why.t: Butter melts when it gets warm. A dot of butter at the far end of a rod slides off when the heat reaches it.

rodrace.model: a model: the real order, sped up
rodrace.predictLine: 2. Predict: which butter dot falls off first?
rodrace.needPredict: Put every butter dot on 1st, 2nd or 3rd first.
rodrace.tooMany: Pick only {n}. Tap one you picked to take it out.
rodrace.needMix: Race again with at least one metal rod AND one rod that is not metal.

rods.note: Steel carried heat, too, but more slowly.

rodrace.q: Which rods carried the heat fastest?

opts.t: The metal rods. Metals are heat conductors.
They all carried heat the same.
opts.miss: Look at your race table. Did all the butter fall at once?

rodrace.win: Metals carry heat fast (conductors). Glass and wood slow it down (insulators). Clue 3!

cuprace.title: The Cup Race
todo: Tap the cup you think stays warmest.
Press Start and watch the graph.
Then rank the cups.

why.q: How do I read the graph?
why.t: Each line is one cup. The higher the line, the warmer the water. A line that drops fast means the cup lost heat fast.

cuprace.predictQ: Which cup will keep the water warm the longest? Tap one.
cuprace.needPredict: Predict first: tap the cup you think stays warmest.
cuprace.rankLine: Rank the cups: drag each one onto a place (or tap it, then a place).
cuprace.rankMiss: Look at the graph again. Where did the {c} line end?
cuprace.q: Which cup is the best insulator?

opts.miss: Look at the graph. Whose line dropped fastest?
Close! But whose line stayed highest?

cuprace.win: The foam cup slowed the heat the most. The metal cup let it out fastest. Clue 4!

iceblocks.title: Ice on two blocks
todo: Touch both blocks.
Check them with a thermometer.
Predict, then drop the ice cubes.
iceblocks.sameWhy: They sat in the same room, so they are the same temperature. The metal only FELT colder.
iceblocks.predictQ: Put an ice cube on each block. Which ice cube melts first?
iceblocks.needPredict: Predict first: which ice cube melts first?
iceblocks.fastLine: The ice on the {b} melted first.
iceblocks.whyLine: Metal is a conductor, so it carries the room’s heat into the ice fast. That’s also why it felt cold: it carried YOUR heat away from your hand fast. The plastic slowed the heat down, so its ice is still there.
iceblocks.done: Wow! The block that feels coldest melts ice the fastest.

mugdesign.title: Design Rosa’s new mug
todo: Pick the mug, a lid and the handle.
Run the 30-minute parade test.
Keep changing things until it gets the APPROVED stamp.

why.q: What makes a good parade mug?
why.t: After 30 minutes in 54°F air, the cocoa should still be hot (120°F or more), and the handle must be safe to hold.

mugdesign.needAll: Pick a mug, a lid choice and a handle first.
mugdesign.burnLine: The metal handle on a metal mug got too hot to hold!
mugdesign.tryLine: Change one thing and test again.
mugdesign.win: Rosa’s new mug keeps the cocoa hot AND is safe to hold. Insulators win!

snowcoat.title: The coat on the snow cone
todo: Guess which snow cone melts FIRST.
Put them in the sun.
Read why.
snowcoat.model: a model: a hot afternoon at Palmetto Beach
snowcoat.guessQ: Four snow cones sit in the hot beach sun. Which one melts FIRST?
snowcoat.needGuess: Guess first: which one melts FIRST?
snowcoat.wrongPre: Surprise! The coat didn’t warm it up.
snowcoat.whyLine: The puffy coat kept its snow cone frozen the LONGEST. A coat doesn’t make heat. Its trapped air slows heat down, so the beach’s heat gets IN slowly. In winter, a coat slows YOUR heat from getting OUT.
snowcoat.win: Coats don’t make heat. They slow it down!

snowcoat.tease: Wrap a snow cone in a puffy coat and set it in the sun. What happens?

tool.name: Infrared thermometer
tool.teaser: Read a temperature without touching anything.

why.t: Every warm thing gives off invisible light called infrared. This tool catches that light and shows the temperature, without touching. The red dot is just for aiming.

irtherm.title: Aim, pull, read
todo: Drag the red dot onto something in the photo (or tap a dashed circle).
Pull the trigger and read the screen.
Try both photos. On the shiny mug, try the tape trick.

photo.alt: A hand holding a real infrared thermometer. Its screen reads 28.5 degrees Celsius.
photo.cap: A real infrared thermometer. Photo: Cjp24, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

irtherm.tapeBtn: 🩹 Stick tape on the shiny mug
irtherm.missLine: Aim the red dot right on something first.
irtherm.shinyLine: That can’t be right! The mug was just in hot water. Shiny metal acts like a mirror, so the thermometer reads mostly the light bouncing off it. Scientists stick tape on shiny metal. Press the tape button.
irtherm.tapeLine: Tape on! Aim at the tape and pull the trigger again.

q.q: The iron armrest and the wooden seat read almost the same. Why does the iron FEEL hotter?

opts.t: Iron is a conductor, so it moves heat into your hand much faster.
opts.why: Right! A metal slide in the sun burns for the same reason: it pours heat into your skin fast.

opts.t: The iron is much hotter than the wood.
opts.why: Check your readings: 98°F and 95°F are close.
It read the shiny mug right once the tape was on.

hlCoach.title: Highlight like a scientist
tips: Highlight key words, not whole paragraphs.
If everything is yellow, nothing stands out. Aim for a few words in each paragraph.
Look for words that are explained.
Bold words, and words followed by “means”, “is called” or a meaning in ( ), are often worth saving.
Look for answers to the Big Question.
Ask yourself: does this help me explain which way heat moves, or why metal feels cold and wood doesn’t?
“Because”, “so” and “first … then” show how ideas connect.
Yellow = important. Green = evidence I might use in my answer. Pink = something I wonder about.

practice.q: Practice: tap the 3 to 5 words that matter most in this sentence.
practice.text: Heat always moves from a warmer object to a cooler one, and insulators slow it down.
practice.model: A scientist might highlight “heat”, “warmer”, “cooler” and “insulators slow”. Those words hold the big idea.

hlCoach.outside: This works in every subject. When you read anything, save the words that answer your question, and skip the rest.
